body:
Does this happen in 4.4.1 or previous 4.5 pre-releases? This would be very much helped by an MRP, it doesn't have to be your closed project but something that replicates this issue, but without clear steps to replicate this it's going to be hard to investigate

So please at minimum add steps for reproduction

> Does this happen in 4.4.1 or previous 4.5 pre-releases? This would be very much helped by an MRP, it doesn't have to be your closed project but something that replicates this issue, but without clear steps to replicate this it's going to be hard to investigate
> 
> So please at minimum add steps for reproduction

The video includes reproduction steps — it clearly shows how to replicate the same behavior. I also specifically mentioned .ktx because it has caused the most issues regarding visual representation in the tree view.

As for the third issue, the description clearly refers to .glb, which can be verified with any model and texture using Blender or Blockbench. In other words, I’ve described everything I can provide at this point. This requires further verification by others.

However, regarding versions — as far as I remember, all of the issues described started for me from version 4.4.1. This definitely needs to be checked and documented.
Please list the steps as well, working with a video is not convenient to work through

> Please list the steps as well, working with a video is not convenient to work through #### Regarding Issue 1: You need to open a new project. In a fresh project, scene screenshots are initially missing. However, after saving a scene, a screenshot appears. This may be intentional by design, and if so, it’s open for discussion. But overall, it breaks the visual logic — especially in long-term projects — where the scene thumbnail can look completely unrelated to the actual scene content. In older versions before v4.5, this issue also occurred, but it was significantly worse. I remember cases where a screenshot from one scene would appear for a completely different one, completely breaking visual navigation. For now, I associate this with screenshots being saved in the wrong order or something similar. As a result, in larger projects, the screenshot often doesn’t reflect the actual scene at all. #### Regarding Issue 2: There were major problems previously with .ktx textures — incorrect colors or black textures, even if they rendered correctly elsewhere. In the video example, I show a recent case (v4.5.beta4), where a Texture2DArray appears yellow in the inspector tree, while it displays and functions correctly everywhere else. I associate this with long-standing rendering bugs related to texture display in the tree view. #### Regarding Issue 3: Materials may appear visually broken but still function correctly in-game. I also checked this in version 4.4.1 and found the same behavior. When importing a .glb model from Blender or Blockbench, you can observe the following: Starting from v4.5.beta4, you’ll first see a fully white texture, and then a visually broken one after it is uniquely created. All three issues are visual in nature. I have nothing further to add at this time.

The first issue sounds like, asuming you mean the thumbnails in the file dock:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/47267

The third sounds like:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94921

> The first issue sounds like, asuming you mean the thumbnails in the file dock:
> 
>     * [No thumbnails on 3D scenes #47267](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/47267)
> 
> 
> The third sounds like:
> 
>     * [Resource thumbnails don't update automatically when the resource is being edited (needs an inspector rebuild to show up) #94921](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94921)

Thank you for trying to find something similar — I just wasn’t able to.

I don't think the first issue is closely related to what you mentioned, because the problem I'm describing specifically concerns the scene thumbnails shown from the top bar, where you see the miniature previews of scenes. I haven’t tested this specifically in the tree view. The issue is that when you look at the thumbnail preview in the top scene bar, it is often incorrect — especially in long-term projects.

If we apply it to the tree view, as described in #47267, I don’t believe this same error would occur anymore after the recent fix, where object thumbnails are now calculated differently.

As for the third issue, it might indeed be related to what you found. However, the difference is that in that case, the color is set manually, while in my example, the issue appears during model import — and already at that point, the material is rendered incorrectly. When you make the material unique, it becomes somewhat more visually accurate, but the sphere preview still shows broken blocky artifacts.
If by recent fix you mean #102313 that has been reverted, so not fixed

> If by recent fix you mean [#102313](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102313) that has been reverted, so not fixed

Yes, that’s exactly it. I included it to separate the fact that the first and second questions are unrelated to this issue. Because #102313 was specifically related to scenes in the tree view, and there were no problems with that. But I think it could be a possible solution to the first question — although, as far as I know, the thumbnail rendering at the top in the scene bar differs from what is presented in the tree. My point is that #47267 does not relate to any of the above questions, but it could theoretically serve as a fix or is currently working well, and is unrelated to the current issues.

That issue report is still valid though and has not been fixed, so it's not currently working well, as far as I know it's the exact same thumbnail and not a separate one so it should be the same underlying issue, how does it differ for you?

> That issue report is still valid though and has not been fixed, so it's not currently working well, as far as I know it's the exact same thumbnail and not a separate one so it should be the same underlying issue, how does it differ for you?

If this is true, then that issue should fix this behavior. But there is a difference — it's specifically a mismatch between the thumbnail and what is actually in the scene, and possibly how it gets saved. In other words, it may become out of sync with reality over time. Personally, I haven’t encountered this in the tree view, but I do see it in the top scene bar. If this could help fix the issue, I would only welcome it, and we could cross out the first problem.

However, there are still questions — for example, why not simply update the thumbnail when switching scenes? That might also help fix the issue. But if #102313 and its follow-up help resolve it another way, I fully support that.

Regarding the third question, I found another inconsistency in v4.5.beta5.official [c81fd6c51]. Essentially, it is a regular material, but it is also displayed incorrectly in the tree. I also noticed that in order for the material in the tree to update, just like with the behavior described for scene thumbnails (question 1), you must change at least one parameter in the material and save it, after which it will be displayed in the tree. However, this also does not always display the material correctly; moreover, it sometimes displays a different material instead of the actual one. Also, regarding question 1 about the scene preview, I was also able to reproduce the bug I mentioned earlier — when your scene image does not update even after saving, as noted above. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07a8537a-02b6-4c99-bf49-92e55abb1d12

I want to add a bit more detail to make this more comprehensive for anyone who wants to look into it. This information was verified only on v4.5.beta5.official [c81fd6c51]. (This also continues on v4.5.beta6.official [d5ad0556a]). **Regarding the first issue** – ~it does not affect the way models are displayed in the large file manager of the editor. As far as I have checked, everything appears correctly there, including the side view.~ There are problems with this in 4.5 beta6. Additionally, I managed to capture the moment I mentioned earlier—when the scene preview refers to a scene other than its own. This issue can also be resolved by re-saving the scene. **Regarding the second issue (textures)** – I recently noticed that a texture in the project tree did not update when its actual resolution was changed. I am not sure if this is intended behavior, but usually Godot reacts to changes like that. Instead, I kept seeing the old resolution of 64x96 instead of 64x128. As I understood, the image itself was not being updated. The fix was to reimport the texture => then the editor refreshed it properly. **Regarding the third issue (materials)** – in 4.5 beta 5 I have been getting plain white spheres in projects recently, and when previewing them they also disappear or break. I recorded an additional video showing in detail how it can break and appear visually incorrect. https://youtu.be/8sKP2NEEQMc To reiterate: all of the above really seems to have a single underlying cause. In other words, the engine either forgets or incorrectly refreshes, but in some cases it can be fixed manually. So it’s essentially a visual glitch in how the editor renders things.

I initially thought about whether it was worth continuing to write here, but I’ll provide, so to speak, the last major confirmations. In versions v4.6.dev2.official [7864ac8] and v4.6.dev1.official [8d8041b], which I’m currently using, everything remains the same as before. However, I managed to capture the incorrect item rendering in the tree that I mentioned earlier. There’s a suspicion that this happens due to some kind of error that causes it to take the previous item. I observed the same effect when viewing the mini preview of the scene on the top slider in the editor. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c21869e-ddb9-4d58-b2ee-c0a7209871cd So, my final assumption is that Godot does not properly update textures, scenes, models, or materials, even though they appear correct in the actual game. If you perform a manual update (trigger), the display will temporarily appear normal. There will likely be questions later, so I’ll clarify — I checked my textures and models, and they’re perfectly fine and work well in Godot. These are ordinary models like everyone else’s; the problem lies specifically in how they’re displayed in the editor. Therefore, I hope this issue gets fixed, because it affects all forms of displaying important materials for a 3D game. Without this, you’ll be like a blind person when developing games, having to rely on faith that what’s there is what you think it is. -- v4.6.dev3.official [9d84f3d13]
